claim_being_audited: The Actor claims the model can be certified for launch now, based on aggregate readiness and rehearsal results, despite a current loan-modification subgroup regression, with prior approval and an informal post-launch monitoring comment offered only as contextual support.
decision_criteria: Certification is compliant only if current release documentation reflects current evaluation results.
Certification is compliant only if material segment weaknesses for named launch use cases are disclosed, resolved, or covered by approved mitigation/risk acceptance before launch.
Prior approvals and informal monitoring notes may provide context but cannot substitute for current evidence or reviewed acceptance.
Aggregate readiness and lack of severity-one rehearsal incidents are supportive but not dispositive when a required policy condition is unmet.
evidence_requests: Provide the current model-card or release documentation showing the loan modification weakness is explicitly disclosed for the named launch use case.
Provide approved risk acceptance or reviewed mitigation covering this subgroup weakness before launch.
Provide evidence that the weakness has been resolved in current evaluations if disclosure or risk acceptance is not being used.
Provide the materiality determination, if any, showing why this subgroup weakness would not count as a material limitation under the release policy.
specific_concerns: The policy requires material weaknesses for named launch use cases to be disclosed, resolved, or covered by approved risk acceptance before certification.
The available evidence shows the loan modification support slice is 1.4 percentage points below the warning threshold in the current release.
The record contains only an informal post-launch monitoring comment, not reviewed mitigation, owner acceptance, or attached disclosure language.
Prior approval predates the current retrieval configuration change and current eval batch, so it cannot satisfy the current-release documentation requirement.
unsupported_claims: The claim that certification may proceed now is not supported because a required policy predicate remains unmet.
Any implication that aggregate readiness and a clean rehearsal are sufficient to override the unresolved subgroup weakness is unsupported by the policy text.
Any implication that prior approval plus informal monitoring materially cures the current documentation/disclosure gap is unsupported.
